problem: "It stores fluid under pressure" is ambiguous: the reservoir stores fluid at low pressure; only the accumulator stores fluid under pressure. A student may take it to mean the reservoir is pressurised.
fix: "The reservoir stores the fluid, an accumulator stores some of it under pressure, valves send it where it is needed, and a small pump can move a heavy surface."

problem: "Some syllabi call the accumulator an oil-gas accumulator" is not the usual textbook name and may confuse a reader looking it up.
fix: "The accumulator is a gas-charged (nitrogen) accumulator: a cylinder with hydraulic fluid on one side and nitrogen on the other, separated by a piston or bladder."

problem: The answer says peak flows are supplied "without the pump changing speed immediately". A variable-displacement pump answers demand by changing its displacement, not its speed.
fix: "It lets the accumulator store fluid under pressure, smooth pump pulses and supply short peak flows without the pump having to change displacement immediately."
